questions.question: Your cell phone rings while you are driving and you do not have a hands-free device. What should you do?

options.text: Answer the call because it may be an emergency.
Let the call go to voicemail.
Check the incoming number before answering the call.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the call go to voicemail.
questions.explanation: Do not use a cell phone while driving without a hands-free device. For minors, using any cell phone while driving is illegal, except in emergencies. Even with a hands-free device, it is best to let calls go to voicemail while driving to avoid distractions.

questions.question: A vehicle is stopped on the right shoulder with its hazard lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left and speed up.
Slow down and pass very carefully.
Stop your vehicle until you can see what has happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass very carefully.
questions.explanation: When you see hazard lights ahead, slow down. There may be an accident or emergency. Offer help if asked, or pass very carefully.

questions.question: When must drivers use their seat belt?

options.text: Unless they are driving a vehicle built before 1978.
Unless they are driving a limousine.
Always. Not wearing one will result in a traffic ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. Not wearing one will result in a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always wear seat belts. You can be ticketed if you do not.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
When one lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
When one vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions are more likely when one driver moves faster or slower than other vehicles on the road. Driving faster than traffic increases your risk of a crash. Driving slower than traffic can also be dangerous because it may cause rear-end collisions or other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibrations and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the travel lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibrations and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the travel lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic signal.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon merge into one lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
The speed you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates drivers behind you, causing them to make dangerous passing moves. It is safest to drive with the flow of traffic and within the speed limit.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more alcohol, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: Saves time so you get to your destination more quickly.
Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is one of the most common causes of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: Fog lights only.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: It is best to wait until fog clears before driving. If you must drive in fog, drive slowly and use your windshield wipers and low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does a blue painted curb mean?

options.text: Parking is allowed for no longer than 15 minutes.
Parking is only allowed when picking up or dropping off passengers.
Parking is for disabled persons with a special placard or plate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking is for disabled persons with a special placard or plate.
questions.explanation: A blue curb is for parking only by disabled persons or drivers of disabled persons who display a disability placard or license plate.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and the ability to concentrate.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down when approaching this signal.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to yield to any vehicle or pedestrian in the intersection. You may proceed carefully only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and watch for other vehicles.
Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be alert before entering the intersection. Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles in the intersection. You do not need to stop for a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: You must tell the DMV within five days if you:

options.text: Get a traffic ticket.
Sell or give your vehicle to someone else.
Paint your vehicle a new color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sell or give your vehicle to someone else.
questions.explanation: You must contact the DMV within five days when you sell or transfer your vehicle to another person.

questions.question: Which is against the law?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, at railroad crossings, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings or where signs say no passing.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal before you move.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal to alert other drivers before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before any move to the left or right.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry.
Slow down traffic.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. When you see cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests, slow down and follow their directions.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn at other cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the next car.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your car if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your car if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your car. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of fast traffic.

questions.question: What usually causes a locked wheel skid?

options.text: Braking too hard when going slowly.
Braking gently when going slowly.
Braking too hard when going fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking too hard when going fast.
questions.explanation: A locked wheel skid usually happens when a driver brakes too hard while driving fast. Always use your brakes smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: You just sold your car. You must tell the DMV within ____ days.

options.text: Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Five
questions.explanation: When you sell or transfer a vehicle, you must tell the DMV within five days.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes:

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Always look carefully for motorcycles before changing lanes because:

options.text: They are small and hard to see.
They always have the right-of-way at intersections.
It is illegal for motorcycles to share lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are small and hard to see.
questions.explanation: Check carefully for motorcycles when changing lanes because their small size makes them easy to miss and they can hide in your blind spots.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: If you have a green light but traffic blocks the intersection, you should:

options.text: Wait outside the intersection until it clears.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
Change lanes and drive around the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until it clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
Change lanes, go slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is raised. Do not move until you are sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe to move.

questions.question: You should turn on your headlights:

options.text: One half hour after sunset.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.
When parked at a school.

questions.correctAnswerText: One half hour after sunset.
questions.explanation: Use headlights one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, when using windshield wipers, and anytime visibility is less than 1,000 feet.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest thing to do is get out of their way. Do not try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off the precipitation and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: In California, you must file a crash report with the DMV when:

options.text: The crash causes $1,000 or more in damage.
You plan to leave the state for more than 30 days.
You refinance your car loan.

questions.correctAnswerText: The crash causes $1,000 or more in damage.
questions.explanation: If a crash results in death, any injury, or more than $1,000 in damage, you must file a report with the DMV within 10 days. Your insurance agent or lawyer can file the report for you.
